title: Lifecycle event payload fields consumers depend on
answers: What properties does an error tracking lifecycle event carry?
Why does the manual event omit exception_timestamp?
body:
Built in `logic/lifecycle_events.py:prepare_issue_lifecycle_event`; must match cymbal's ingestion producer so destination property filters work on both paths.
- Props: `name`, `description`, `issue_description` (duplicate of description, compat), `first_seen` (created_at ISO), `severity`, `status` (display label from `status_label`, same casing as cymbal), `fingerprint` (only if present; chosen by `_issue_fingerprint_for_links`: oldest first_seen then id), `assignee` (only if currently assigned), `previous_status` (status transitions), `previous_assignee` (unassign only), `merged_issue_ids`/`split_issue_ids` (string lists).
- `exception_timestamp` deliberately omitted for manual events (scene falls back to latest exception).
- Identity: `distinct_id` = issue id, `uuid` = `notification_id` (also names the alert delivery workflow -> idempotent redelivery).
- `person` is minimal (id, distinct_id, email, first_name); default webhook body sends `{person}` verbatim, so don't add fields.
- `temporal/alerts/types.py:AlertDeliveryWorkflowInputs` is slimmer: string status/assignee, actor_email, severity, fingerprint, first_seen; merge/split ids reduced to `merged_count`/`split_count` in `extra`. `temporal/alerts/filtering.py` (`LIFECYCLE_PROPERTY_KEYS`, `alert_filters_match`) reads these; keys include name, description, issue_description, first_seen, severity, status, exception_timestamp, fingerprint, assignee.
applies: Adding/renaming payload fields requires checking alert filters and Temporal inputs; not for ingestion-side events.
